channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Riemann hypothesis proof explained: how the Lean proof was verified
item.description: A proof of the Riemann hypothesis that Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he found working with Claude was checked line by line by computer programs within a day, but the official prize still needs a published paper, two years and the agreement of mathematicians.

item.title: Uber safety features for riders explained: PIN, recording, teens
item.description: Uber's app already has a ride PIN, trip sharing, crash and detour checks and audio recording for every rider, and in November 2026 it started testing video-recorded rides and rides for children as young as 10 in a few US cities.

item.title: USB port with a battery symbol: what it means and how to turn it off
item.description: A small battery or lightning bolt next to a laptop's USB port usually marks a port that can charge your phone or earbuds, on some laptops even while the lid is closed or the laptop is off.

item.title: 1Password hacked: names and emails taken, passwords and vaults safe
item.description: 1Password says an attacker got into an employee's work GitHub account on 19 November and downloaded account records for some customers, including names and email addresses. Vault contents, the keys that protect them and recovery keys weren't accessed.

item.title: Adobe Acrobat Chrome extension linked to heavy SSD writes on a Windows PC
item.description: A Reddit user found Chrome had written over 300GB in about three days on a mostly idle Windows 11 PC and traced it to the Adobe Acrobat extension; after removing it, idle writes dropped by more than 81%.

item.title: CardKeeper: business card scanner app for iPhone, no account
item.description: CardKeeper scans the front and back of a business card, reads the details on your iPhone and keeps both sides together with your notes. The $0.99 app came out on 24 November and was #38 among paid Business apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Carry saves ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok chats as Markdown files
item.description: Carry is a Chrome and Edge extension that backs up your chats, projects and files from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok as Markdown files in a folder you pick on your computer. You can search the saved chats and continue one in another AI.

item.title: ChangeLens Earth: satellite before and after app for any place
item.description: ChangeLens Earth lets you pick any place and two dates, then drag a divider across free satellite images to see what changed, from a new neighborhood to a shrinking glacier. The $0.99 iPhone and iPad app was #54 among paid Navigation apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: ChatGPT usage limits: Chat and Work now share one meter
item.description: OpenAI has started merging ChatGPT's Chat and Work into one place with a single usage allowance, beginning with a small group of Pro subscribers on 25 November. Its help page says Plus, Pro and Business plans share one allowance across ChatGPT and Codex from December.

item.title: Claude Opus 5.6 rumors: testers say Anthropic is trying a new model
item.description: Some Claude users on X say their chats were answered by an unannounced model they call Opus 5.6, according to posts gathered by TestingCatalog on 24 and 25 November. Anthropic hasn't announced or confirmed it.

item.title: Cloud identification app Cielo names cloud types from your camera
item.description: Cielo, a $3.99 iPhone and iPad app, estimates which type of cloud is in the sky from your live camera, a photo or a saved video. It was #35 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Cue by Manus: AI assistant app that books, orders and plans for you
item.description: Cue, an iPhone app from Manus maker Butterfly Effect, is an AI helper that can use apps you allow to plan trips, order food and book things, with you confirming each payment. It was #97 among free Productivity apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Deevo prayer journal app for iPhone keeps entries on your phone
item.description: Deevo is a devotional journal for prayer, Scripture and reflection, with guided templates, prayer lists and an offline King James Bible. The $1.99 iPhone app came out on 23 November and was #95 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: DooDay poop tracker app: one tap logs a bowel movement on iPhone
item.description: DooDay: Poop Tracker is a 1.99-dollar iPhone and iPad app where you tap "I Pooped!" to log a bowel movement and look back over a calendar. It came out on 22 November and was #63 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: DoodleYak drawing app for kids and adults: no ads or in-app purchases
item.description: DoodleYak is a 5.99 dollar drawing and painting app for all ages on iPhone, iPad and Apple silicon Macs, with brushes, stamps, mirror drawing and coloring pages. Out since 5 November, it was #25 among paid Graphics and Design apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Dosee pill reminder app for iPhone: vitamins and medication in one list
item.description: Dosee, a pill reminder and tracker for iPhone and iPad out since 23 November, keeps your vitamins, supplements and medications in one list and logs each dose with one tap. It costs $5.99 once, with no subscription.

item.title: Gemini shopping help on Android: compare prices, warranty and returns
item.description: Gemini's floating overlay on Android can now help while you shop: open it over a shopping app or website and it offers three buttons, Help me pick, Compare prices, and Check warranty and returns. It's rolling out now, and Android Police links the timing to Black Friday in the US.

item.title: Hark Pro AI assistant app: books tables and orders groceries for you
item.description: Hark Pro, a free AI assistant app for iPhone and iPad from Hark Labs, can log in to websites for you and finish tasks there, such as booking a table on OpenTable or ordering food through DoorDash, with your approval. On 25 November it was #12 among free Lifestyle apps on the US App Store.

item.title: Infrared Developer: infrared photo editor app for iPhone and iPad
item.description: Infrared Developer is a $12.99 photo editor for infrared pictures, doing on a phone what usually takes custom camera profiles in desktop RAW software. It was #87 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: iPad with macOS: Apple tests it internally, no release planned, Gurman says
item.description: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says on his Power On podcast that Apple has had iPads running macOS inside the company for some time, but that no work is under way to release it to customers. Apple hasn't commented.

item.title: iPhone storage full before the holidays: iCloud vs Google Photos
item.description: When your iPhone storage is full of photos, iCloud Photos with Optimize iPhone Storage and Google Photos' Free up space can both move the full-size pictures to the cloud, but each counts against a free limit, 5 GB at Apple and 15 GB at Google, and deleting works differently in each.

item.title: Jidaria wallpaper app: calm 4K wallpapers for iPhone and Mac
item.description: Jidaria, out since 24 November, is a collection of hundreds of calm wallpapers, each in one version for the iPhone screen and one in 4K for the Mac. It costs $2.99 once for both.

item.title: Learn AI app for beginners: So That's AI explains it in 134 lessons
item.description: So That's AI, out since 24 November for iPhone and iPad, is an illustrated beginner's guide to artificial intelligence in 13 chapters and 134 lessons. It costs $4.99.

item.title: LightCue: RGB LED strip remote app for iPhone, no account needed
item.description: LightCue is a $2.99 iPhone and iPad remote for Bluetooth LED strips, light bars and bulbs that work with ELK-BLEDOM controllers. It was #97 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Monitor refresh rate stuck at 60Hz: how to check it on Windows and Mac
item.description: A monitor sold as 120Hz or 144Hz only runs that fast when the computer is set to it, and the Refresh Rate setting in Windows or macOS shows what yours uses; if the higher number is missing, the cable, the port or the driver is often the limit.

item.title: New Apple Health app explained: Insights, Longevity and Health Age
item.description: The new Apple Health app comes with iOS 27.3, which 9to5Mac expects in December: it adds an Insights tab with daily summaries, a Longevity tab with a Health Age score and at-home movement checks, but only on an iPhone 15 Pro or newer with Apple Intelligence turned on.

item.title: Notes from the Field: journal app for iPhone, iPad and Mac with paper look
item.description: Notes from the Field is a 4.99 dollar journal app with leather-style covers, white pages and a page-curl effect for iPhone, iPad and Apple silicon Macs. It came out on 20 November and was #58 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: PhraseLab MIDI composer app writes chords, melody and bass
item.description: PhraseLab builds a chord progression, melody, bassline and arpeggio that fit together once you choose a key, a scale and one of 32 genres. The $14.99 iPhone and iPad app came out on 23 November and was #61 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: PTO tracker app PTO Balance forecasts your paid time off on iPhone
item.description: PTO Balance, a $1.99 iPhone and iPad app, adds the hours you earn each payday to your time-off balance and shows how planned days off change it months ahead. It was #71 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Putty Buddy: 3D sculpting app for iPhone and iPad with STL export
item.description: Putty Buddy lets you sculpt digital clay and build 3D models with your fingers on iPhone and iPad, then export them as STL or OBJ files. It costs $1.99 once and was #40 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Raycast browser extension 2.0 lets Raycast AI fill forms on Mac
item.description: Raycast 2.14 for Mac adds Browser Use: its AI can open pages, fill in forms and pull information from your tabs, bookmarks and history in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, in the background. It came out on 25 November and needs version 2.0 of Raycast's browser extension.

item.title: Samsung battery health dropping after One UI 9: fix due in One UI 9.5
item.description: Samsung support told a Galaxy owner that the fast drop in battery health some people see since One UI 9.0 will be addressed in the One UI 9.5 update. One owner says some phones show 94% battery health after about a month of use.

item.title: Singing Santa Apple Watch face: tap and Santa dances and sings
item.description: Singing Santa Watchface is a 1.99-dollar Apple Watch app with a Santa in a Christmas scene who dances and sings a Christmas song when you tap the screen. It came out on 22 November and was #52 among paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Sony a6700 app for beginners: Camera Academy teaches the camera in 15 lessons
item.description: Sony a6700 Camera Academy is a new $1.99 iPhone and iPad app with 15 beginner lessons you work through with the camera in your hands. It was #86 among paid Education apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Synchronus 91 organ app for iPad and iPhone: tonewheel organ without samples
item.description: Synchronus 91 is a 12.99 dollar organ app for iPad and iPhone that models a classic 91-tonewheel console organ and a rotary speaker in real time instead of playing recordings. Out since 6 November, it was #45 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: WhatsApp schedule message feature rolling out: send texts up to 14 days later
item.description: WhatsApp now lets you schedule a message by holding the send button and picking a date and time, from 10 minutes to 14 days ahead. It works in one-to-one and group chats, for text, photos and videos, and is rolling out worldwide over the coming weeks.

item.title: WhatsApp sound stickers in testing: stickers that play audio on tap
item.description: WhatsApp is testing stickers with sound in its Android beta 2.26.41.3, according to WABetaInfo: you turn a video into a sticker and keep its audio, record a voice note or add a sound file from your phone. WhatsApp hasn't said when, or whether, everyone gets it.

item.title: Zombies Aren't Real game: zombie defense on real city maps for iPhone
item.description: Zombies Aren't Real is a $4.99 strategy game where you fight a zombie outbreak on maps built from real-world map data, street by street. It came out on 23 November and was #73 among paid apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Claude install as app: turn Artifacts into Mac and Windows desktop apps
item.description: Claude can now install an Artifact you built in chat as its own app on a Mac or Windows PC, with an icon and window that open outside Claude. It's a beta for all plans, including free accounts.

item.title: 2 billion passwords leaked in open infostealer database, ExpressVPN says
item.description: About 2 billion stolen logins, mostly from password-stealing malware, sat in a database anyone could open without a password, security researcher Jeremiah Fowler found. ExpressVPN published his report on 24 November.

item.title: Android Auto black screen: Google Maps not loading for some drivers
item.description: Some Android Auto users report that Google Maps doesn't load when Android Auto starts, so the car's screen shows black where the map should be. Most reports come from Ford owners, and Google hasn't commented yet.

item.title: Apple Watch voice recorder app Tapkeep turns your day into text
item.description: Tapkeep records your day from an Apple Watch with one tap, then turns the audio into text on your iPhone, split into titled conversations you can search. It costs $9.99 once with no subscription, and was #86 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: AreaMap: land area measure app for iPhone shows acres and lot lines
item.description: AreaMap measures a piece of land when you tap its corners on a satellite map or walk its edge with GPS, and shows county lot lines. The free iPhone and iPad app was #36 in Utilities on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Buy now pay later on Black Friday: fees, interest and credit scores
item.description: Buy now pay later splits a purchase into payments: pay-in-4 plans from PayPal, Afterpay and Affirm charge no interest, monthly plans can cost up to about 36% a year, and whether a plan shows up on your credit report depends on the company.

item.title: CBeebies shows on Netflix from 2 December in a new hub
item.description: The BBC is putting 24 CBeebies preschool shows, including Hey Duggee, Numberblocks and Teletubbies, in their own hub on Netflix from 2 December in the UK, Ireland, the US, Canada and Australia, as a six-month trial.

item.title: ChatGPT flight search: Dohop's WAYA plugin finds bookable flights
item.description: Travel company Dohop added its WAYA flight search to ChatGPT: you pick a direct or multi-airline trip in the chat, then book it on the airline's own checkout page, where you can add seats and bags.

item.title: Duo Remote: remote desktop iPhone app for Windows PCs and Macs
item.description: Duo Remote is a new $1.99 iPhone app that shows and controls your Windows PC over Remote Desktop or your Mac over its built-in Screen Sharing. It was #99 in paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Encrypted RCS messaging between iPhone and Android explained
item.description: Texts between iPhones and Android phones can be end-to-end encrypted since Apple and Google started rolling it out in beta on 11 May 2026, but only over RCS, with iOS 26.5 or later, the latest Google Messages and a supported carrier.

item.title: First Light: sunrise alarm app for iPhone using your HomeKit lights
item.description: First Light fades your dimmable HomeKit lights up from red to daylight each morning, so you wake without an alarm sound. It costs 3.99 dollars once and was #87 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 24 November.

item.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra camera downgrade leak: no laser autofocus or 3x zoom
item.description: Leaker Ice Universe says Samsung will remove the laser autofocus from the Galaxy S27 Ultra, and he and OnLeaks both expect the 3x telephoto camera to go, leaving three rear cameras. Samsung hasn't confirmed either.
